sec: Hypokalemia · causes tree, cellular shifts and clinical features

items.q: Match each renal branch of the hypokalemia tree with what sits under it — 1) Renal with acidosis 2) Renal with alkalosis and raised blood pressure 3) Renal with alkalosis and normal blood pressure … A) RTA type 1 and RTA type 2 B) Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, Liddle's syndrome, AME and GRA C) Bartter's and Gitelman's syndromes
items.exp: The renal side splits by acid-base status, and the alkalosis limb then splits by blood pressure, with the five endocrine hypertensive causes on one side and Bartter's and Gitelman's on the other. (Book p971)

items.q: In what order are the endocrine hypertensive causes of renal potassium wasting listed?
opts: Conn's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, Liddle's syndrome, apparent mineralocorticoid excess, glucocorticoid remediable aldosteronism
Cushing's syndrome, Conn's syndrome, Liddle's syndrome, glucocorticoid remediable aldosteronism, apparent mineralocorticoid excess
Liddle's syndrome, Conn's syndrome, apparent mineralocorticoid excess, Cushing's syndrome, Bartter's syndrome
Conn's syndrome, Gitelman's syndrome, Liddle's syndrome, Cushing's syndrome, apparent mineralocorticoid excess
items.exp: The list runs 1 Conn's syndrome (PHA), 2 Cushing's syndrome, 3 Liddle's syndrome, 4 AME and 5 GRA, with the full form of GRA given as glucocorticoid remediable aldosteronism. (Book p971)

items.q: All of these are grouped under the non-renal, cellular-shift branch EXCEPT:
opts: Insulin given during diabetic ketoacidosis treatment
items.exp: The shift branch carries insulin in DKA therapy, alkalosis, drugs, barium intoxication, hypokalemic periodic paralysis and VIPoma-related gut loss; Conn's syndrome sits in the renal alkalosis-with-hypertension limb. (Book p971)

items.q: Fill up: The drug list under cellular shift reads beta-2 agonists, alpha antagonists, theophylline, ______ and ______, the last entry being annotated with thiazides far exceeding furosemide.
items.exp: The five drug entries are beta-2 agonists, alpha antagonists, theophylline, chloroquine and diuretics, with diuretic hypokalemia graded as thiazides much greater than furosemide. (Book p971)

items.q: Assess two shift-branch items: I Hypokalemic periodic paralysis is annotated as a calcium-channel disorder. II The diuretic entry is placed under cellular shift even though the same potassium loss is produced in the tubule.
items.exp: The page prints hypokalemic periodic paralysis as a Ca2+ channelopathy, and it does list diuretics inside the shift branch, a filing that reflects the book's grouping rather than the renal-wasting mechanism usually taught. (Book p971)

items.q: A 54-year-old has 3 weeks of profuse watery diarrhoea, potassium 2.4 mEq/L, achlorhydria and a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis. Which named entity and which limb of the tree does this page use?
opts: VIPoma causing WDHA syndrome, under non-renal gastrointestinal loss
Bartter's syndrome, under renal alkalosis with normal blood pressure
Primary hyperaldosteronism, under renal alkalosis with hypertension
Distal renal tubular acidosis, under renal acidosis
items.exp: The GI loss entry is VIPoma with the WDHA label, described as watery diarrhoea, hypochlorhydric acidosis, hypokalemia and a normal anion gap hypokalemic acidosis. (Book p971)

items.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four bullet features listed for the VIPoma entry?
items.exp: The four bullets are watery diarrhoea, hypochlorhydric acidosis, hypokalemia and NAGMA; blood pressure is not part of this description. (Book p971)

items.q: Match each magnesium-related statement with its consequence as written — 1) Magnesium regulates 2) Hypomagnesemia produces 3) Low magnesium is caused by … A) Aminoglycosides, cisplatin and proton pump inhibitors B) The ROMK channel C) Potassium leak out and therefore hypokalemia
items.exp: Magnesium regulates ROMK, its deficiency lets potassium leak out through that channel, and the three named causes are aminoglycosides, cisplatin and proton pump inhibitors. (Book p971)

items.q: Assess the dietary limb of the tree: I Inadequate potassium intake is explicitly labelled rare. II Inadequate magnesium intake is listed as a second dietary cause of hypokalemia.
items.exp: The diet branch carries only two entries, inadequate K+ intake with the annotation rare and inadequate Mg2+ intake. (Book p971)

items.q: Every one of these is shown in the box that raises serum potassium EXCEPT:
items.exp: The potassium-raising box holds acidosis, hyperglycemia, beta-2 blockers, alpha agonists, raised osmolality and exercise, while beta-2 agonists belong to the box that lowers serum potassium with insulin, alkalosis and alpha antagonists. (Book p971)

items.q: Fill up: In the shift diagram, insulin, alkalosis and alpha-adrenoceptor ______ move potassium into the cell, while acidosis, exercise and a rise in ______ move it out.
items.exp: The fall-in-serum-K+ box lists insulin, beta-2 agonists, alkalosis and alpha antagonists; the increase box lists acidosis, hyperglycemia, beta blockers, alpha agonists, raised osmolality and exercise. (Book p971)

items.q: All of the following are listed as clinical features of hypokalemia EXCEPT:
opts: Spastic quadriparesis with cranial nerve palsy
items.exp: The page describes an ascending flaccid areflexic quadriparesis with sphincters and cranial nerves spared, not a spastic palsy with cranial nerve involvement. (Book p971)

items.q: Fill up: The weakness of hypokalemia is described as ______ with bladder and bowel involvement, and an ______ ascending flaccid areflexic quadriparesis in which the sphincters and cranial nerves are spared.
items.exp: The bullets read weakness with the abbreviation B/D, followed by B/I areflexic ascending flaccid quadriparesis with sphincters and cranial nerve spared. (Book p971)

items.q: On the K+ deficit graph for chronic hypokalemia, a serum potassium of about 2 mEq/L corresponds to a total body deficit closest to which range?
items.exp: The dashed lines drop from about 675 on the deficit axis to a serum K+ near 2, and the curve is steep at low values, showing how far serum potassium underestimates the true deficit. (Book p971)

items.q: Assess what the deficit curve implies: I Serum potassium and total body deficit are related non-linearly, so a modest-looking serum value can hide a large deficit. II The graph shows the deficit as roughly constant across the 1.5 to 4 mEq/L range.
items.exp: The plot falls from about 1200 mmol at a serum K+ near 1.5 towards zero at 4 mEq/L, so the relationship is markedly curved rather than flat. (Book p971)

items.q: Which two endocrine or metabolic features close the clinical list on this page?
opts: Insulin resistance and worsening of hypertension
Insulin deficiency and falling blood pressure
items.exp: The last two bullets are insulin resistance and worsening of hypertension, alongside arrhythmias with torsades, colonic pseudo-obstruction and chronic tubulointerstitial disease. (Book p971)
